messages.subject: Longitudinal CFA
parts:
Dear All,

I am a newbie in Lavaan and trying to do Longitudinal Comfirmatory Factor Analysis. 

I have twenty one indicators that explain for three latent variables over 3 time points.

Actually my goal is to get factor score from the model. But I am not sure how to handle this. 

I tried to run a model for each time points and I will get a set factor score. If I do it for 3 time points, I will get three sets factor score.

My questions is can we get only one set factor score from a model of 3-latent variables over 3 time points? 

Could you give me an example how to handle the problem like this?

Thank you in advance.

best regards

Yenni

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Longitudinal CFA
parts: I tried to run a model for each time points and I will get a set factor score.
Per time point (one from each model)
If I do it for 3 time points, I will get three sets factor score.

Again, 1 per time point.  This is consistent with your model: you have 3 factors.  It is the same factor at each time point, but it is still measured repeatedly, so you get factor scores for each time you measure it.
My questions is can we get only one set factor score from a model of 3-latent variables over 3 time points?

By fitting a one-factor model for all items at all timepoints.  But I don't think that is an accurate representation of your data-generating process.  People change, so their factor scores should change (not that estimated factor scores are a robust way to estimate change over time).
